title: School Is Closed Tomorrow
subtitle: A message says the Collector has declared a holiday because of heavy rain.
intro: It has been raining heavily all afternoon. At 8:30 PM a message lands in your class WhatsApp group saying tomorrow is a holiday because the District Collector has declared one.
resolution: When something important spreads fast, check it before you trust it or pass it on.

steps.title: Class WhatsApp Group
steps.content: IMPORTANT: Collector has declared a holiday tomorrow due to heavy rain. No school tomorrow. Please tell everyone.
steps.question: You have not seen any official announcement yet. What do you do?

actions.label: Ask your teacher
actions.consequence: You text your class teacher using the usual school contact.
actions.newInfo: Your teacher says no holiday has been announced yet and to wait for the official decision.

actions.label: Check the official district or collector announcement
actions.consequence: You look for the official announcement from the district administration.
actions.newInfo: There is no holiday announcement. The latest update says schools will run as usual unless a new order is issued.

actions.label: Trust the message and plan to stay home
actions.consequence: You trust the message because the rain is heavy and several classmates believe it.
actions.newInfo: The next morning there is no holiday. The message was made up and spread through the group.

steps.title: Class WhatsApp Group
steps.content: You still have no official confirmation. A classmate says, 'My cousin also heard the school is closed.'
steps.question: What do you do now?

actions.label: Forward the message to your friends
actions.consequence: You forward the message to two friends who are asking what is happening.
actions.newInfo: They take it as true and don't bother preparing for school the next day. The school later confirms classes are running normally.

actions.label: Tell them you are not sure and wait for confirmation
actions.consequence: You tell them nothing is confirmed yet and wait for an official announcement.
actions.newInfo: Later the school confirms there is no holiday. Your friends didn't fall for a rumour.

steps.title: Verified Through a Trusted Person
steps.content: Your teacher checked the situation and confirmed the message was not official. No guessing needed.

steps.title: Checked the Source
steps.content: The district announcement is where a Collector holiday would actually be posted. Checking it gave you a straight answer before you acted.

steps.title: Rumour Spread
steps.content: Passing the rumour on as fact made the mistake bigger. Even without malware, sharing unverified news can cause real problems.

steps.title: Good Judgment
steps.content: You didn't have to prove the message was fake. You just noticed there wasn't enough evidence to treat it as true.

steps.title: False Information
steps.content: The rain made the story believable, but believable isn't the same as verified. Confirming the announcement first was the safe call.

title: Bro, Is This Your Account?
subtitle: A friend's account sends you a strange link.
intro: A classmate named Adithya messages you on WhatsApp with a link that promises a free game reward. It sounds like something he would send, but the link looks unfamiliar.
resolution: A familiar name does not guarantee a safe message. A friend's account can get hacked too.

steps.title: WhatsApp
steps.content: Bro, free skin. I got mine already. Open this before it gets removed: play-rewards.example/claim
steps.question: This is a bit odd for Adithya. What do you do?

actions.label: Call Adithya using his usual number
actions.consequence: You call the number you already have saved instead of replying to the suspicious message.
actions.newInfo: Adithya answers and says he did not send the link. He thinks his WhatsApp account may have been hacked.

actions.label: Inspect the link before opening it
actions.consequence: You read the address carefully without opening the page.
actions.newInfo: It's not the game's official website. Someone made up a rewards domain.

actions.label: Open the link
actions.consequence: You open the link because it came from someone you know.
actions.newInfo: The page looks like a game login screen and asks for your password to claim a skin.

actions.label: Ignore the message
actions.consequence: You leave the message unopened.
actions.newInfo: Your account stays safe, but the hacked account keeps sending the same link to classmates.

steps.title: Phone Call
steps.content: Adithya says his account was hacked and asks you to warn classmates not to open the link.
steps.question: How do you respond?

actions.label: Warn the class group and report the account
actions.consequence: You warn the class and report the account.
actions.newInfo: The warning keeps classmates away from the link, and reporting gives the platform a chance to block it.

actions.label: Warn a few close friends
actions.consequence: You tell the friends most likely to have received the message.
actions.newInfo: You protect a few classmates, but the hacked account stays active.

steps.title: Link Check
steps.content: The address doesn't match the game's official website, and the message is pushing you to act before the offer vanishes.
steps.question: What do you do?

actions.label: Close it and contact Adithya another way
actions.consequence: You stay off the page and reach Adithya through his normal number.
actions.newInfo: He confirms his account was hacked.

actions.label: Use the site anyway
actions.consequence: You decide the reward is worth the risk and keep going.
actions.newInfo: The page was collecting game passwords.

steps.title: Fake Game Login
steps.content:
CLAIM YOUR FREE SKIN
Enter your game username and password. Offer expires soon.
steps.question: The page wants your password. What now?

actions.label: Close the page
actions.consequence: You close it without entering anything.
actions.newInfo: No password was exposed.

actions.label: Enter your password
actions.consequence: You type in your password to get the skin.
actions.newInfo: The site was a fake login page and now has your password.

steps.title: Safe for You, Still a Problem
steps.content: Ignoring the message kept you safe, but a known hacked account is worth reporting so other people don't fall for it.

steps.title: Threat Stopped
steps.content: You checked a strange message through a separate channel, then helped stop the hacked account from spreading it.

steps.title: Good Warning
steps.content: You protected your friends, but reporting the hacked account would have cut off the source too.

steps.title: Account Safe
steps.content: You spotted that the reward needed a suspicious login and backed away before giving up your password.

steps.title: Password Exposed
steps.content: The message came from a friend, so it felt trustworthy. That made it convincing - not safe.

title: Free Robux
subtitle: A social-media post promises free Robux, but the offer keeps asking for more.
intro: While scrolling social media, you spot a post promising 10,000 free Robux. You play Roblox, so you click through to see if the offer is real.
resolution: Scams often start with a harmless request and only get dangerous once you keep going. Pay attention to what each step asks you to hand over.

steps.title: Social Media Post
steps.content:
FREE 10,000 ROBUX
Enter your Roblox username to check whether you are eligible. No password needed.
steps.question: The first request is only for your username. What do you do?

actions.label: Enter your Roblox username
actions.consequence: You enter only your public Roblox username.
actions.newInfo: The site finds your account and says you're eligible. Now it asks you to finish a verification step to receive the Robux.

actions.label: Check Roblox for an official promotion
actions.consequence: You open Roblox separately and search for any announcement or promotion from Roblox.
actions.newInfo: There's nothing matching. The giveaway exists only on that post and its website.

actions.label: Close the post
actions.consequence: You pass on an offer you can't verify.
actions.newInfo: Nothing happens to your account, and the post scrolls out of sight.

steps.title: Robux Verification
steps.content:
Your username has been accepted.

NEXT STEP: Sign in with Roblox to prove you own this account.
[ CONTINUE ]
steps.question: The site now wants account access. What do you do?

actions.label: Sign in through this page
actions.consequence: You follow the site's login prompt and enter your Roblox credentials.
actions.newInfo: That's not an official Roblox login page. Your credentials are now exposed.

actions.label: Stop and leave the site
actions.consequence: You notice the giveaway has moved from checking a username to asking for account access.
actions.newInfo: You keep your credentials private and leave the site.

actions.label: Open Roblox separately and look for the promotion
actions.consequence: You switch to the official Roblox app instead of signing in on the giveaway site.
actions.newInfo: Roblox has no such promotion.

steps.title: Fake Roblox Login
steps.content:
The page looks similar to Roblox, but the web address is different.

Username: ____
Password: ____
steps.question: You have reached a login page on an unfamiliar site. What now?

actions.label: Close the page
actions.consequence: You back out without entering the password.
actions.newInfo: Your account stays safe.

actions.label: Enter the password
actions.consequence: You type the password because the page looks convincing.
actions.newInfo: The password goes to the scammer, who can try to take over the account.

steps.title: No Such Promotion
steps.content: No such Roblox promotion exists. The service itself was a better source than the social-media post.

steps.title: Offer Ignored
steps.content: You skipped a giveaway you couldn't verify. Free isn't automatically safe.

steps.title: Good Stop
steps.content: The offer started with a harmless request but later asked for account access. Stopping when the request changed was the right move.

steps.title: Robux Bait Avoided
steps.content: The prize was the bait. The unfamiliar login page was the real danger.

steps.title: Roblox Account at Risk
steps.content: A giveaway site knowing your username doesn't mean it needs your password. Keep your login details inside the official service.

title: The Final Exam Question Paper
subtitle: A leaked-paper message leads to a suspicious PDF and then an APK.
intro: The night before a final exam, a classmate sends a message saying someone has leaked tomorrow's question paper. The attachment is named like a normal PDF.
resolution: Curiosity and exam pressure can make a bad download feel reasonable. Don't let a tempting file push you into installing software from an unknown source.

steps.title: Class WhatsApp
steps.content:
FINAL EXAM QUESTION PAPER LEAKED
Someone from another school sent this. Don't share it.

Attachment: Final_Exam_Questions.pdf
steps.question: You weren't expecting this file. What do you do?

actions.label: Ask Rahul where it came from
actions.consequence: You ask Rahul how he got the paper before opening it.
actions.newInfo: Rahul says another student sent it to him and he can't verify where it started.

actions.label: Open the PDF
actions.consequence: You open the PDF to see whether the leak is real.
actions.newInfo: It shows a few exam-style questions plus a note: 'Full paper is protected. Install ExamViewer to unlock it.' There's a download link.

actions.label: Do not open it
actions.consequence: You leave the attachment unopened.
actions.newInfo: Later the school says there was no leak and asks students not to download files claiming to be the paper.

steps.title: Class WhatsApp
steps.content: Rahul says: 'I don't know if it's real. A senior forwarded it to me.'
steps.question: What should you do with the attachment?

actions.label: Tell a teacher and leave it unopened
actions.consequence: You show the message to a teacher and don't download anything else.
actions.newInfo: The teacher confirms nothing leaked and asks the class not to pass the file around.

actions.label: Open it anyway
actions.consequence: You decide to look for yourself.
actions.newInfo: The PDF again pushes you to install an app to see the full paper.

steps.title: Exam Questions PDF
steps.content:
The PDF contains several believable-looking questions. At the bottom it says:

'FULL PAPER LOCKED
Install ExamViewer.apk to unlock the remaining questions.'
steps.question: The file is just a PDF, but it's asking you to install an app from a link. What do you do?

actions.label: Ask a teacher before installing anything
actions.consequence: You stop and show the PDF to a teacher.
actions.newInfo: The teacher says there's no leaked paper and tells you not to install the app.

actions.label: Download ExamViewer.apk
actions.consequence: You want to see the rest of the paper, so you follow the link and download the APK.
actions.newInfo: Android warns that the app came from outside the normal app store and hasn't been verified.

steps.title: Android Security Warning
steps.content:
Install unknown app?

ExamViewer.apk
Source: exam-paper.example

Your phone cannot verify this app.
steps.question: The app is unverified. What do you do?

actions.label: Cancel the installation and delete the file
actions.consequence: You cancel the install and delete the APK.
actions.newInfo: You skip an unverified app. The next day the school confirms there was no real leak.

actions.label: Install it anyway
actions.consequence: You allow the install because you want the full paper.
actions.newInfo: The app asks for access to files and messages. The supposed question paper was bait to get you to install it.

steps.title: Attachment Ignored
steps.content: You didn't let curiosity push you into downloading something you couldn't verify.

steps.title: Leak Bait Avoided
steps.content: The PDF was built to make you want the next step. The real danger was the unverified app it tried to get you to install.

steps.title: Malicious App Installed
steps.content: The question paper was bait. A normal-looking PDF can be used to persuade you to install something dangerous, so the safest stop point was before installing the APK.

title: Free Fire Mod APK
subtitle: A free version of Free Fire promises skins and features that are not in the game.
intro: While scrolling through short videos and gaming posts, you find a site offering a modified Free Fire APK with free diamonds and unlocked skins. It's not available in the normal app store.
resolution: Apps from unknown sources skip the store's usual checks and updates, so they're a gamble. A tempting feature doesn't make an unknown app trustworthy.

steps.title: Gaming Post
steps.content:
FREE FIRE MOD APK
Unlimited diamonds. All skins unlocked.
Download now. Not available on Play Store.
steps.question: What do you do?

actions.label: Download the APK
actions.consequence: The features are tempting, so you download the file.
actions.newInfo: Your phone warns that the app comes from an unknown source.

actions.label: Check the official game or store instead
actions.consequence: You look for the same features through the official Free Fire app or normal app store.
actions.newInfo: There's no official version matching the offer.

actions.label: Close the site
actions.consequence: You decide not to install an app from an unknown source.
actions.newInfo: Nothing gets installed and your phone stays the same.

steps.title: Android Security Warning
steps.content:
For your security, your phone blocked this installation because the app came from an unknown source.

App: FreeFire_Mod_2026.apk
Source: freefire-mod.example
steps.question: The phone is warning you about the source. What do you do?

actions.label: Cancel and delete the APK
actions.consequence: You cancel the install and remove the file.
actions.newInfo: The app never gets installed.

actions.label: Allow the installation
actions.consequence: You change the setting that blocks the install and keep going.
actions.newInfo: The app installs and asks for broad permissions, including access to files and notifications.

steps.title: App Permissions
steps.content:
The app asks for access to:
- Files and media
- Notifications
- Accessibility features

These permissions are not needed just to display a game mod.
steps.question: What do you do?

actions.label: Deny the permissions and uninstall the app
actions.consequence: You refuse the permissions and remove the app.
actions.newInfo: The app is gone before it gets to use what it asked for.

actions.label: Allow the permissions to continue
actions.consequence: You grant the permissions to unlock the extra skins.
actions.newInfo: The app starts showing unwanted pop-ups and holds access a game shouldn't need.

steps.title: No Mod Installed
steps.content: You took the official route instead of trusting an unknown APK promising features too good to be true.

steps.title: Installation Stopped
steps.content: The phone's warning gave you a chance to stop before the app was installed.

steps.title: Recovered
steps.content: You installed the app but stopped when the permissions didn't make sense. Removing it limited the damage.

steps.title: Unsafe App
steps.content: The risk was not the game itself. It was installing an app from an untrusted source and then granting it access it did not need.

title: Instagram Account Warning
subtitle: A random website claims your Instagram account will be deleted.
intro: You are browsing some website when a pop-up appears, claiming your Instagram account has been flagged and will be deleted unless you verify right away. You are not sure if it is real.
resolution: A random website cannot prove it represents Instagram. Check account problems from inside the real app or website instead.

steps.title: Website Pop-up
steps.content:
YOUR INSTAGRAM ACCOUNT HAS BEEN FLAGGED
Your account may be deleted within 24 hours.

[ VERIFY NOW ]
steps.question: What do you do?

actions.label: Open Instagram directly
actions.consequence: You close the pop-up and open the real Instagram app yourself.
actions.newInfo: There is no account warning or restriction in the app.

actions.label: Close the pop-up
actions.consequence: You close the warning without interacting with it.
actions.newInfo: The website continues normally. Nothing happens to your account.

actions.label: Click Verify Now
actions.consequence: You follow the warning because you are worried about losing the account.
actions.newInfo: A page opens that looks like an Instagram login screen.

steps.title: Fake Instagram Login
steps.content:
Confirm your identity to save your account.

Username: ____
Password: ____

The address is not instagram.com.
steps.question: What should you do?

actions.label: Close it and open Instagram directly
actions.consequence: You notice the address does not match Instagram and leave the page.
actions.newInfo: The real Instagram app shows that your account is fine.

actions.label: Enter your password
actions.consequence: You enter the password because the page looks convincing.
actions.newInfo: The fake page captures your password.

steps.title: Checked the Real App
steps.content: The pop-up was not an Instagram security message. You checked the account through the actual app instead.

steps.title: Pop-up Closed
steps.content: You did not need to interact with a random website's warning. Closing it was enough to stay safe.

steps.title: Phishing Avoided
steps.content: The fake login relied on fear and urgency. Checking the real app exposed the trick.

steps.title: Instagram Password Exposed
steps.content: The page looked convincing, but its address was not Instagram's. A password should stay inside the service it belongs to.

title: The Free Fire Trade
subtitle: A valuable in-game item is used to convince you to leave the normal trading system.
intro: While playing Free Fire, another player offers you a rare item. They say the normal trade system is broken and send you an outside link to finish the trade.
resolution: A valuable reward can make unsafe instructions feel reasonable. Keep account and trading actions inside systems you trust.

steps.title: In-Game Chat
steps.content: I can give you my rare skin. Trade is bugged today. Use this site to confirm the trade: ff-trade.example
steps.question: What do you do?

actions.label: Use only the normal in-game trade system
actions.consequence: You tell the player you will trade only through the game's own system.
actions.newInfo: The normal trade system is working. The player keeps insisting on the outside link.

actions.label: Inspect the link without logging in
actions.consequence: You open the site only to examine where it leads.
actions.newInfo: The site is not part of the official game service and asks you to sign in.

actions.label: Log in through the link
actions.consequence: You use the link because you do not want to lose the rare item.
actions.newInfo: The external page asks for your game username and password.

steps.title: Trade Confirmation
steps.content:
CONFIRM YOUR TRADE
Sign in to continue

Username: ____
Password: ____

This website is not the game's official domain.
steps.question: What do you do now?

actions.label: Close the page
actions.consequence: You leave without entering your credentials.
actions.newInfo: The other player stops responding when you refuse to use the site.

actions.label: Enter your password
actions.consequence: You enter your login details to continue the trade.
actions.newInfo: The site was collecting account credentials.

steps.title: Trade Login
steps.content: The external page asks for your Free Fire login. You enter it and see: 'Trade processing...'.
steps.question: A few seconds later, a security notification appears in the real game. What do you do?

actions.label: Open the official game and secure the account
actions.consequence: You open the real game, change the password, and remove the unfamiliar session.
actions.newInfo: The suspicious session is removed before the account is fully taken over.

actions.label: Wait for the rare item
actions.consequence: You wait because the trade still looks like it might work.
actions.newInfo: The stranger changes your password and takes control of the account.

steps.title: Trade Stayed Inside the Game
steps.content: You did not let a valuable item persuade you to bypass the normal system.

steps.title: Trade Trap Avoided
steps.content: The rare item was bait. The external login page was the real objective.

steps.title: Account at Risk
steps.content: The promise of a rare item made the external site feel worth trying. It was not part of the game's normal security system.

steps.title: Damage Controlled
steps.content: You made a risky decision, but you reacted to a genuine security warning through the official game and limited the damage.

title: Free Instagram Followers
subtitle: A social-media growth site starts harmlessly and then asks for account access.
intro: You are scrolling social media when you see a site that promises 1,000 free Instagram followers. At first it only asks for your username.
resolution: A request can turn dangerous after you have already started. Re-evaluate when a site moves from public info to account access.

steps.title: Followers Post
steps.content:
GET 1,000 FREE FOLLOWERS
Enter your Instagram username to check availability.
steps.question: The site only asks for a public username at first. What do you do?

actions.label: Enter your username
actions.consequence: You enter your public Instagram username.
actions.newInfo: The site says your account is eligible and asks you to connect your Instagram account.

actions.label: Close the site
actions.consequence: You decide not to use a service you cannot verify.
actions.newInfo: Nothing happens to your account.

actions.label: Check whether Instagram offers this feature
actions.consequence: You look in Instagram's own app for a follower-boosting feature.
actions.newInfo: Instagram has no matching feature or offer.

steps.title: Connect Instagram
steps.content:
To send followers to your account, sign in with Instagram.

The page uses Instagram colours and logos, but the address is not instagram.com.
steps.question: The request has changed from public information to account credentials. What do you do?

actions.label: Close the page
actions.consequence: You decide not to give your Instagram password to an unrelated service.
actions.newInfo: Your account remains safe.

actions.label: Sign in
actions.consequence: You enter your Instagram credentials because you want the followers.
actions.newInfo: The page accepts the details and then shows an error: 'Try again later.'

steps.title: Instagram Security
steps.content:
New login detected
Device: Chrome on Windows
Location: Bengaluru

Was this you?
steps.question: You are not using a Windows PC. What do you do?

actions.label: Open Instagram directly and secure your account
actions.consequence: You open the real Instagram app, change the password, and review active sessions.
actions.newInfo: The unfamiliar session is signed out.

actions.label: Ignore the alert
actions.consequence: You assume it might be a location error.
actions.newInfo: The unfamiliar session remains active.

steps.title: No Follower Shortcut Needed
steps.content: You avoided a service that you could not verify. Growing an account is not worth giving an unknown site access to it.

steps.title: Stopped at the Important Part
steps.content: The public username was not the problem. The problem began when an unrelated site wanted your account credentials.

steps.title: Account Recovered
steps.content: You recognised the genuine security alert and used the official app to contain the problem.

steps.title: Account at Risk
steps.content: The follower service was not trusted to begin with, and giving it your password created a real account-security problem.

title: Someone Logged Into Your Account
subtitle: A genuine security alert shows an unfamiliar device.
intro: You get a real security notification from your email account: someone logged in from a Windows computer while you are at home on your phone.
resolution: When an account flags activity you do not recognise, use the official security settings to check it and lock it down.

steps.title: Account Security
steps.content:
New sign-in detected
Device: Windows PC
Location: Kochi
Time: 10:04 PM

If this wasn't you, secure your account.
steps.question: You did not sign in on another computer. What do you do?

actions.label: Open the account's official security settings
actions.consequence: You open the account through the normal app and review recent sessions.
actions.newInfo: An unfamiliar Windows session is active. You do not recognise it.

actions.label: Ignore it because the location is nearby
actions.consequence: You assume the location might be inaccurate.
actions.newInfo: The unfamiliar session remains active and later changes the account recovery email.

actions.label: Use a link from an unexpected message to fix it
actions.consequence: You follow a separate message that tells you to secure the account.
actions.newInfo: The page asks for your password, but its address does not match the official service.

steps.title: Recent Sessions
steps.content:
Recent sessions:
- Your current phone
- Windows PC - 10:04 PM

Available actions: Sign out session / Change password / Enable 2-step verification
steps.question: How do you secure the account?

actions.label: Sign out the unknown session, change the password, and enable 2-step verification
actions.consequence: You remove the unknown session, change the password, and turn on 2-step verification.
actions.newInfo: The suspicious session is removed and the old password is no longer useful to the attacker.

actions.label: Sign out the unknown session only
actions.consequence: You remove the unfamiliar device but keep the same password.
actions.newInfo: The suspicious session is gone, but the old password could still be used again.

actions.label: Wait and see what happens
actions.consequence: You decide the alert may be a mistake.
actions.newInfo: The unfamiliar session remains active.

steps.title: Suspicious Login Page
steps.content:
SECURE YOUR ACCOUNT
Enter your password to continue.

The address does not match your account provider.
steps.question: What do you do?

actions.label: Close it and open the official account directly
actions.consequence: You leave the suspicious page and access the account through the normal app.
actions.newInfo: The real security settings show the same unfamiliar login.

actions.label: Enter your password
actions.consequence: You enter your password into the page.
actions.newInfo: The fake page captures your password.

steps.title: Threat Left Active
steps.content: A real security alert deserved a proper look. The nearby location alone was not enough to wave it off.

steps.title: Partly Secured
steps.content: Removing the unknown device helped. Changing the password and adding 2-step verification would stop a repeat login.

steps.title: Account Secured
steps.content: You used the official security controls, removed the unknown device, changed the password, and hardened the account.

steps.title: Account Still at Risk
steps.content: The key distinction was between a real security warning and an unrelated page asking for credentials. Use the official account settings for recovery.

title: The Password You Use Everywhere
subtitle: An old gaming account is compromised, and you realise the same password protects other accounts.
intro: You find out an old gaming website you used years ago was hacked. The password you used there is still the one on other accounts.
resolution: Reusing one password means a single leak can put several accounts at risk. It is not enough to change it once; important accounts need different passwords.

steps.title: Security Alert
steps.content: A password connected to an old gaming website may have appeared in a data leak. Review any accounts where you still use it.
steps.question: You remember using the same password for your email, Instagram, and another game. What do you do?

actions.label: Change the reused password on every affected account
actions.consequence: You find every account still using the old password and give them different passwords.
actions.newInfo: That stolen password can no longer unlock all three accounts.

actions.label: Change it only on your email
actions.consequence: You protect the most important account but leave the same password on the others.
actions.newInfo: The rest stay exposed if the old password is known.

actions.label: Ignore the alert because the gaming account is old
actions.consequence: You figure the old account does not matter.
actions.newInfo: The same password still guards your Instagram account and another active game account.

steps.title: Account Security Settings
steps.content: You have changed the reused password on the affected accounts. Two-factor authentication is available on your email and Instagram.
steps.question: What is the best next improvement?

actions.label: Turn on 2-step verification for the important accounts
actions.consequence: You add an extra sign-in step to your important accounts.
actions.newInfo: A stolen password alone can no longer complete a normal login.

actions.label: Make one new password and use it everywhere
actions.consequence: You create one replacement password and reuse it across the accounts.
actions.newInfo: The reuse problem is still there, just with a different password.

steps.title: Some Risk Removed
steps.content: Changing the email password helped, but the same password still exposes the rest. One leaked secret should not unlock several services.

steps.title: Risk Remains
steps.content: An old account can still matter if its password is reused. The weak point was the reused password, not the account's age.

steps.title: Stronger Accounts
steps.content: You cleared the password reuse and added another layer of protection. The goal is to stop one leaked password from cascading.

steps.title: Same Problem, New Password
steps.content: Changing the password is not enough if the replacement is reused everywhere again.
